title: Mechanical protective effect of lens anterior capsule disc on corneal endothelial cells during femtosecond laser-assisted cataract surgery in a rabbit model

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: 'licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License', link https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/; CC0 waiver for data made available in the article)

indication: Healthy adult New Zealand white rabbits (right eyes, 2.5-3.0 kg, free of ocular disease); experimental model of ultrasound endothelial injury during femtosecond laser-assisted lens surgery, not a clinical cataract population

groups.description: Experimental (LACD) group: LenSx femtosecond capsulotomy (6 mm), the isolated lens anterior capsule disc lifted against the endothelium with DisCoVisc OVD, then 1 min of 80% longitudinal phaco ultrasound (10-s bursts, tip 1.5-2.0 mm from the endothelium, I/A 12 cc/min, vacuum 300 mmHg, intracameral heparin), followed by I/A removal of disc, OVD and lens material; eyes whose disc separated from the endothelium during the ultrasound exposure were excluded (Methods). Topical tobramycin/dexamethasone 4x/day for 7 days.

Control (conventional FLACS) group: the same femtosecond capsulotomy, ultrasound exposure and aftercare, except that the isolated disc was removed once the main corneal incision was created (no endothelial protection by the disc).

exclusions.what: Table 1 (endothelial cell count and endothelial cell loss)
Slit-lamp corneal edema descriptions in Results (diffuse/focal edema counts and resolution days)
exclusions.reason: Counts and qualitative grades, not CCT values

notes: Species rabbit: LACD (isolated capsulotomy disc protection) is the investigational technique (treated); conventional FLACS without the disc is the standard arm (control).

Non-clinical injury model: deliberate 1-min 80% longitudinal ultrasound aimed at the endothelium with altered fluidics (I/A 12 cc/min, vacuum 300 mmHg, heparin); rabbit lenses are soft and clear; animals were sacrificed after day 7.

Experimental-group eyes whose disc detached during the ultrasound exposure were excluded by an intraoperative criterion (Methods, Discussion), not by a postoperative outcome; two eyes with decentered attached discs remained in the experimental group (Results).
Group sizes are 20 rabbits (right eyes) per group from Methods; Table 2 gives no per-visit n.
